titulo: Will AI Coding Eat Video Game Engines?
resumo: When Travis McGeathy’s studio, Seeker Entertainment, ran out of funding in September, its game KinForge went down with it. KinForge was an online game built in Unreal Engine 5.7 and designed to run on servers hosted by Amazon Web Services (AWS). With no one left to pay the server bill, the game became unplayable even for those few developers, including studio co-founder McGeathy, who had the code. Then, on a whim, McGeathy pointed Anthropic’s Claude Code at the project and asked it to make KinForge playable without AWS. After four hours of mostly hands-off work he had a build that let players host their own games. Claude added support for peer-to-peer play over both the Internet and a local area network. To McGeathy’s surprise, it also added persistent save states, a feature that lets players resume a game if they’re disconnected. Although KinForge is still built in Unreal Engine, developments like this could give companies that create game engines cause for concern. titulo: NGINX2Root: Remote Code Execution vulnerabilities in nginx
resumo: Xint is reporting that it has discovered a collection of five critical vulnerabilities in the NGINX web server. The worst flaw, it says, would allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute commands on an affected nginx server with HTTP/2 enabled . The company also reports a local-privilege escalation (LPE) kernel vulnerability , which was introduced in the 4.15 kernel, in the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) subsystem. If chained with the NGINX vulnerability, it would allow an attacker to gain root privileges on the host. A kernel patch for this is not yet available. We also obtained a root shell on the host in a setup where nginx was running in a Docker container. On many Linux distributions, the SCTP module is installed by default and the kernel loads it automatically the first time a program opens an SCTP socket. Whether SCTP is reachable on a given host still depends on the kernel, the available modules, and the container's restrictions. Where it is reachable, the attacker can take over the host kernel. titulo: CBD oil offers no behavioral benefit for youths with intellectual disability, new study finds
resumo: Cannabis contains two key compounds that act on the brain: cannabidiol (CBD) and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC). Although both interact with the body's endocannabinoid system, the outcomes of consuming them are poles apart. THC is the compound responsible for marijuana's intoxicating high and can sometimes trigger adverse effects, including psychosis. CBD, on the other hand, is associated with potential anxiety-relieving and anti-inflammatory effects. Despite limited evidence that it works, over the last decade, CBD-rich medical cannabis has gained popularity as a treatment for behavioral problems in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).

titulo: Atoms in sync: Superradiance offers a new kind of frequency comb

The flashes came from billions of atoms embedded in the crystal. Coupled to a tiny superconducting circuit, the atoms had become synchronized and started emitting light together through a special quantum phenomenon known as superradiance.

titulo: Protecting wild bees in Europe through calcareous grassland management and connected habitats
resumo: Calcareous grasslands are wildflower-rich ecosystems that develop on shallow, alkaline, nutrient-poor soils over chalk or limestone bedrock. They are rare and important habitats for wild bees and other pollinators—yet how well they can support these valuable communities depends on how they are managed. An international research team, led by the University of Göttingen, has shown that long-term abandonment or intensive management threatens the diversity of wild bees. Extensive management of these areas, together with appropriate nature conservation measures in the surrounding landscape, is crucial. The findings were published in the Journal of Applied Ecology.

titulo: The beginning of a beautiful friendship? Interaction could be key to human acceptance of robots
resumo: Whether people accept humanoid robots depends not only on what the robots can do for us, but above all on how we experience interacting with them—through all our senses and over time. This is the conclusion of a research team at the University of Potsdam that examined the psychological foundations of humanoid robot acceptance. Technical performance, safety, and the ability to meet human needs are not the only factors that determine acceptance. Instead, acceptance emerges from a dynamic interplay of perception and social interaction, as humans and robots respond to and influence each other.

resumo: The fastest robot to be made entirely of soft materials can reach speeds of up to 4.72 meters—a little more than 5 yards—per second, engineers at the University of California San Diego have shown. The six-legged robot can run on a wide range of terrain, from sand to mulch to concrete. It can also swim in water and walk underwater. The robot, designed, built and tested at the UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering, is 3D-printed in one go using only one material and doesn't need electronics to function.

resumo: MIT researchers have discovered that the brain’s natural waste-removal system becomes significantly less effective during sleep as people age.
